PullRequest.Title: chat: show organization-required plugins from the Copilot runtime as managed
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #347520.

## Context

#347520 added a "Managed by your organization" tag to plugins an organization controls in the Customizations editor, and an error row for a plugin the organization requires that could not be installed ("Your organization requires this plugin, but it isn't installed.").

## Problem

Neither appeared in the main case the feature is for: a plugin required through Copilot managed settings (`enabledPlugins`), viewed in a Copilot (Agent Host) session. The required plugin looked like any other plugin, with no tag, and a required plugin that failed to install was not listed at all.

The cause is where the agent host reads managed state. The Copilot runtime resolves an organization's managed settings for each session. Calling the runtime directly showed:

| Runtime call | Installed required plugin | Required plugin that failed to install |
|---|---|---|
| Global `plugins.list` | listed as an ordinary plugin, no managed state | not listed |
| Session `plugins.list` | `managed`, `managedDesiredEnabled: true` | listed with `installed: false` |

The agent host took managed state from the global list, so it never had any. The tests in #347520 put managed fields on the global list, which the runtime does not do. This is the same on SDK 1.0.33-preview.0 and 1.0.32-preview.3.

Three smaller gaps hid the state even once the host has it:

- When a required plugin fails to install, the runtime reports a warning but no completion, so the host never re-read its plugin inventory.
- A plugin the runtime installed is shown as a local row that hides its agent-host row, and the local row's tag only read the session-free inventory.
- The agent-host plugin item only took organization state from the discovery metadata, which the runtime-installed plugin's publication replaces.

## Fix

Agent host:

- `listPluginInstallations` reads what the organization requires from the chat's own plugin inventory when it has a match, and keeps the global record as the fallback.
- Customization discovery receives the session's plugin inventory and publishes required plugins that have no installed content from it. Discovery still works without a session, with a session that is not ready, and when that call fails.
- A failed managed plugin preparation now signals a runtime plugin change, like a completed one already did.

Workbench:

- An agent-host plugin item reports organization control from its runtime enablement when the host did not publish organization metadata for it.
- The local row of a runtime-installed plugin shows the organization state of its paired session plugin. Its switch already used the paired plugin, so the tag and the locked switch now agree.

Why not use the workbench's own `ChatEnabledPlugins` policy for these rows: that policy can be delivered through channels the runtime does not read, so it could show a plugin as managed when the runtime does not enforce it. The session plugin reports what the runtime enforces. Plugins the workbench loads itself keep using the workbench policy, unchanged.

## How to test

With a `managed-settings.json` that requires an installed plugin and a plugin that does not exist in its marketplace, open Customizations > Plugins in a Copilot session in the Agents window. The installed plugin's row should show the tag with its switch on and disabled. The missing plugin should appear with the tag and the "isn't installed" error.

Component fixture: `chat/aiCustomizations/aiCustomizationManagementEditor/OrgManagedRuntimeInstalledPlugins/{Dark,Light}`.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionCustomizationDiscovery.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentCustomizationItemProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/pluginListWidget.test.ts`: passed (2948 passing, 1 pending). The new and extended tests failed before the fix.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>`: passed, and the pre-commit hygiene check passed.
- New fixture rendered in the Component Explorer (Dark): the runtime-installed required plugin shows the tag and a locked switch, the unmanaged runtime plugin is unchanged, and the missing required plugin shows the tag and an error.
- The compiled discovery from this branch, run against the bundled runtime with a real managed settings file: no row for the missing plugin from the global list alone, and the error row with organization state once it is given the session inventory.

Not verified:

- The full flow in a running build (Agents window, signed in, with the settings file). The host inventory change and the workbench changes are covered by unit tests and the fixture only.
- A plugin the organization blocks (`false` in `enabledPlugins`) against the real runtime.

## Notes for reviewers

- Discovery makes one more runtime call per pass (the session's `plugins.list`) when the session is live.
- Managed state is only known once a chat's session is ready, because that is when the runtime resolves it.
- Not changed here: `setPluginEnabled` on the host still checks the global list for managed state, and the plugin detail page does not show managed state for runtime-installed plugins. The switch in the list is locked through the session plugin.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Every live anchor runs this added await, refreshDiscovery starts all anchors with Promise.all, and each callback targets the same default chat. Tests establish multiple distinct live anchors; only runtime duration and prevalence are uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One logical refresh adds one identical session inventory RPC per live anchor, plus the existing session inventory read in the concurrent runtime-plugin refresh, so cost and concurrency grow as A+1 for A anchors.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive IPC and delayed customization publication
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Anchor discovery read only the global inventory; runtime-plugin refresh performed one session-effective inventory read independent of anchor count.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every anchor discovery now reads the same session-wide inventory, even when there is no missing managed plugin.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 759 adds `await this.managedPluginsWithoutContent(sessionPlugins, plugins, token)` to every anchor's plugin discovery. The callback is wired to the default chat's `listInstalledPlugins()`.
Findings.Title: Coalesce session inventory reads across anchors
Findings.Impact: Managed-plugin completion/failure and plugin installation refreshes issue a concurrent burst of duplicate runtime IPC in sessions with peer chats in different workspaces. Publication waits for all anchor refreshes, delaying the managed-state update when the runtime is slow.
Findings.Evidence: SessionDiscoveredEntry passes `_sessionPlugins` to discovery, one entry exists per unique CustomizationAnchor, and SessionPluginController.refreshDiscovery concurrently refreshes every live anchor together with `_refreshRuntimePlugins()`. The latter calls listPluginInstallations, which already calls the same session's listInstalledPlugins. Per-chat anchor tests demonstrate main, peer-folder, and multi-folder anchors can coexist.
Findings.Recommendation: Fetch the default chat inventory once per controller refresh and share that snapshot with every anchor, or coalesce it in a controller-level promise/cache invalidated by runtime-plugin events.

Scenarios.Scenario: Managed plugin completion or failure refreshes session customizations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A managed-plugin completion or the newly handled failure fires onDidChangeRuntimePlugins, which schedules SessionPluginController.refreshDiscovery. The event callback itself is asynchronous, but the updated customization/plugin view cannot publish until `_refreshRuntimePlugins` and every live anchor refresh finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A newly added calls, one per live anchor, plus the existing call from `_refreshRuntimePlugins`/`listPluginInstallations` when global installations exist
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Anchor discovery did not read the session inventory; runtime-plugin refresh performed one session inventory read independent of A.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All anchor calls must finish before refreshDiscovery publishes the changed customization list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Global plugin inventory and agents/rules/skills/hooks/MCP discovery RPCs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing discovery RPC set once per refreshed anchor
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery RPCs ran before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each anchor already waits for these RPCs before publishing; the diff adds another later session RPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Plugin parsing and customization watcher refreshes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cached plugin parsing where revisions match; discovery work remains per anchor
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing work is awaited with the RPC refresh.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number A of distinct live customization anchors in one agent session. Tests cover a main workspace, a peer workspace, and a multi-folder peer as separate anchor sets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `refreshDiscovery` launches `_refreshRuntimePlugins()` and all A `anchor.refreshDiscovery()` calls in one Promise.all. Each anchor independently reaches the same default chat's session inventory callback; there is no shared limiter or coalesced promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Plugin file contents and discovered directories have caches, but session `plugins.list` has no cache or in-flight coalescing here. All anchors read the same session-wide state. The managed-plugin event is a natural invalidation point that could support one shared snapshot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the same callback, Promise.all fan-out, and duplicate existing inventory read are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime IPC duration and the prevalence of sessions with more than one live anchor are not measured; repository tests prove A can exceed one, so uncertainty lowers severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity boundary fan-out: one session-wide value is redundantly fetched A times and blocks publication.

Scenarios.Scenario: Filesystem-triggered customization rediscovery while editing agents, skills, rules, hooks, or MCP configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A watched change is debounced for 100 ms, then the affected SessionDiscoveredEntry reruns discovery. Its refresh notification and subsequent published customization update wait for discovery, including the newly added session inventory call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One newly added call per debounced discovery pass, even when no managed plugin is missing
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: File-driven anchor discovery used only the global inventory and did not contact the live chat session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after the other discovery RPCs and must complete before the refresh can notify consumers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Watch handling and customization/plugin file reads
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing, bounded by the affected anchor and the 100 ms debounce
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing discovery work remains on the same refresh path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Save/change frequency after per-anchor debounce; effective cardinality is one new session RPC per affected anchor refresh, independent of plugin count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rapid changes in one anchor coalesce through its Delayer/cancellation path. Changes in distinct live anchors remain independent and can run concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Discovered directories are cached and refreshes are debounced, but the session plugin inventory is fetched on every successful discovery pass and has no positive, negative, or in-flight cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added call and placement; medium for user-visible latency magnitude.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical save rates are bounded by debounce and live-session RPC latency is unknown; repeated calls are nevertheless guaranteed for repeated settled edits.
Scenarios.Verdict: The same reported missing-coalescing issue covers this trigger; no separate finding is needed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening, filtering, and rendering the Customizations plugin list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The widget fetches provider items, filters rows, pairs runtime-installed rows with session plugins, and synchronously renders visible metadata, managed tags, ARIA labels, and actions. Marketplace requests remain on their existing asynchronous paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch session customization provider items from the active harness
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached provider fetch per source invalidation/filter generation, same as the previous `getRemotePluginItems` path
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous helper fetched the same provider list, then filtered plugins and search matches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Filtering waits for the same provider result as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged and gated by browse/search mode

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed plugin count I and session plugin count P. Pairing scans P for each relevant installed row, while restrictive searches usually reduce I.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Filter generations discard stale results. ItemProviderItemSource caches one provider promise and coalesces repeated fetches until provider/skill invalidation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider already caches the full item array. The new `sessionPluginItems` array retains references to plugin items before search filtering, but it does not duplicate provider objects and is replaced on each accepted generation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that boundaries are unchanged and retained objects are shared; insufficient evidence for a separate rendering or memory regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large plugin inventories could increase synchronous O(I*P) pairing work, but no repository evidence establishes realistic cardinality high enough for jank.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: provider boundary cardinality is unchanged, retention is bounded/replaced, and the CPU increase is not proven material.

Scenarios.Scenario: Listing runtime plugin installations for host or workbench consumers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The host reads the global plugin inventory, optionally reads the selected live session inventory, reads repository enablement, and maps installation metadata before returning the list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One global and at most one session call per API invocation, unchanged by the metadata selection change
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both existing calls remain awaited before returning inventory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one read per invocation when a file-scheme working directory is available, unchanged

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Global installation count and session plugin count; matching remains collection-based as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The global read precedes the optional live-session read; no new concurrency was introduced in this method.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new inventory cache was added or removed. Runtime plugin contents retain their existing revision cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that no additional boundary or asymptotic work was introduced in this method.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Collection sizes vary, but the diff only selects `managedDesiredEnabled` from an already-fetched matching record.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files. One low-severity boundary-fanout finding was submitted for repeated session inventory IPC across live anchors; workbench rendering, retained plugin references, warning signaling, and installation metadata changes did not independently meet the regression bar.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
